reason: The reading itself is found: packet.js veda 96 --verse 9.58.3 and revision 403221 by action=raw (API 2024-06-19) have dhvasraḥ kaścid rājā puruṣantiḥ kaścit and the Śāṭyāyanaka story (garagirāv iva menāte, etaṃ caturṛcam apaśyatām, asātaṃ sātam abhavad āttam ivaiva na pratigṛhītam); verse.js ok (9.58.3 at [780,3]); entry-check ok. But the plain sense fails the brief’s voice rule that the context clause names the god: it never names Soma, and its opening ‘Its last two verses’ has no antecedent, so under a printed key verse it reads as the verse’s own last two verses. Minor drift: ‘uneasy at so much’ softens the Brāhmaṇa’s ‘thought themselves like swallowers of poison’. Corrected sentence below passes entry-check (44 words).
better: Closing a hymn to Soma, the singers turn to the gifts received; Sāyaṇa, on 9.58.3, takes the givers as kings and cites the Śāṭyāyanaka, where two seers, dreading such wealth like poison, saw this hymn and by it made their gain as if unaccepted.
